# @zakkster/lite-headless/saved-views

A stateful controller for a NAMED collection of view snapshots, an active
view, dirty detection, and optional persistence. GENERIC over any
getState / setState pair -- it captures whatever getState() returns and hands
it back to setState() on apply. The classic "save this filter/sort/layout as
a named view, switch between views, notice when the current state has drifted"
UX of every data grid and dashboard.

Decoupled by design: it pairs naturally with @zakkster/lite-table's
`getViewState()` / `setViewState(view)` seam, but there is NO import, peer, or
devDep on lite-table -- a plain object stub drives the tests. Any state source
that can serialize + restore its own shape works.

## API

```js
import { createSavedViews } from "@zakkster/lite-headless/saved-views";

const sv = createSavedViews({
    getState: () => table.getViewState(),      // REQUIRED function
    setState: (state) => table.setViewState(state), // REQUIRED function
    views:    [],                              // initial {id,name,state}[]
    activeId: null,                            // active view id or null
    storage:  myAdapter,                       // optional { load, save }
    equals:   (a, b) => deepEqual(a, b),       // optional; default JSON compare
    generateId: () => crypto.randomUUID(),     // optional; default per-instance
    onChange:       (views) => {},             // after any collection change
    onActiveChange: (id)    => {},             // after the active id changes
    onApply:        (view)  => {},             // after apply()
});
```

`getState` and `setState` are REQUIRED functions -- construction throws a
TypeError if either is missing or not a function (null is not a function).

## Options

| option         | type                                   | default              |
|----------------|----------------------------------------|----------------------|
| getState       | () => S                                | REQUIRED             |
| setState       | (state: S) => void                     | REQUIRED             |
| views          | { id, name, state }[]                  | []                   |
| activeId       | string \| null                         | null                 |
| storage        | { load(): views\|null, save(views) }   | none                 |
| equals         | (a, b) => boolean                      | JSON.stringify equal |
| generateId     | () => string                           | sv-<instance>-<n>    |
| onChange       | (views) => void                        | none                 |
| onActiveChange | (id \| null) => void                   | none                 |
| onApply        | (view) => void                         | none                 |

## View shape

```js
{
    id:    string,   // unique within the collection
    name:  string,   // human label
    state: any,      // snapshot captured from getState(), stored BY REFERENCE
}
```

Snapshots are stored by reference, never cloned: getState() is expected to
return a FRESH object per call (as lite-table's getViewState() does), so there
is no aliasing between the live state and a saved snapshot.

## Reactive accessors + queries

```js
sv.views()        // SavedView[] in insertion order
sv.activeId()     // string | null
sv.activeView()   // SavedView | null (pull: resolves id against the collection)
sv.getView(id)    // SavedView | null
sv.isDirty()      // boolean -- see below
```

`isDirty()` is PULL-only: `activeView() ? !equals(getState(), activeView().state)
: false`. It is reactive FOR FREE when read inside a computed / effect, because
getState() reads the underlying state signals. There is deliberately NO second
reactive path, and it is NEVER painted in an always-on effect -- that would call
getState() on every underlying-signal change (per-drag-pixel churn). Read it
where you need it (a computed, a paint effect, an event handler).

## Mutations

```js
sv.save(name)       // snapshot getState(); append + set active; returns the view
sv.update(id?)      // overwrite a view's state with getState() (default: active)
sv.apply(id)        // setState(view.state) + set active (does NOT persist)
sv.remove(id)       // drop a view; clears active if it was the removed one
sv.rename(id, name) // rename a view
sv.clearActive()    // active id -> null
```

Fail closed: `save`/`rename` require a non-blank string name; `apply`, `update`,
`remove`, `rename` throw a TypeError on an unknown view id. `update()` with no
argument targets the active view (and throws if there is none).

## Persistence

`storage` is an INJECTABLE, env-agnostic adapter -- NOT hardcoded to
localStorage:

```js
const storage = {
    load: () => JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem("views") || "null"),
    save: (views) => localStorage.setItem("views", JSON.stringify(views)),
};
```

- At construction, if `storage.load()` returns a non-null array it SEEDS the
  collection (overriding `views`). A null return falls back to `views` -- null
  means "nothing persisted", not "empty collection".
- The COLLECTION persists on `save` / `update` / `remove` / `rename`.
- The ACTIVE ID is session state: `apply` / `clearActive` do NOT persist it.
  Persist it yourself from `onActiveChange` if you want it to survive reloads.

## Attach methods

```js
sv.attachRoot(el)         // role=group; data-sv-count + data-sv-active
sv.attachItem(el, id)     // role=option; data-sv-id; click/Enter/Space -> apply(id)
```

## Painted attributes

### Root (attachRoot)
- `role="group"`, `aria-label="Saved views"`
- `data-sv-count="<n>"` -- number of views
- `data-sv-active="<id>"` -- active view id ("" when none)

attachRoot's paint is ZERO-ALLOC: it reads ONLY the count + active-id signals.
It never reads getState()/isDirty(), so an underlying-state change (a column
drag) never fans out into a getViewState() call here. Dirty stays PULL.

### Items (attachItem)
- `role="option"`, `tabindex="0"`
- `data-sv-id="<id>"`
- `data-sv-active` when this item is the active view

## Custom element

`<lite-saved-views>` is PROPERTY-DRIVEN: getState / setState are functions and
cannot be HTML attributes, so it takes NO observed attributes. Wire it in JS:

```js
const el = document.createElement("lite-saved-views");
el.getState = () => table.getViewState();
el.setState = (v) => table.setViewState(v);
el.views    = [];        // optional
el.activeId = null;      // optional
el.storage  = adapter;   // optional
document.body.appendChild(el);

el.savedViews.save("Overdue");   // the live instance (getter)
```

On connect, if `getState` AND `setState` are both functions the element
instantiates and paints role=group via attachRoot(host); otherwise it stays
INERT (no throw). `host.savedViews` (and `host._savedViewsInstance`) expose the
instance for imperative use.

## Composition

- **`@zakkster/lite-table`**: the canonical pairing. `getState` =
  `table.getViewState()`, `setState` = `table.setViewState(view)`. Filters,
  sort, and column layout round-trip as JSON-safe query strings.
- **`lite-menu` / `lite-select`**: a "Views" dropdown listing views(); each row
  is an attachItem, and a "Save current view" action calls save(name).
- **`lite-inline-edit`**: rename a view in place -> rename(id, name).
- **`lite-badge`**: show a "modified" badge bound to isDirty() in a computed.

## Notes

- generateId defaults to a PER-INSTANCE prefix (`sv-<instanceStamp>-<n>`), so
  two controllers sharing one storage adapter never mint colliding ids.
- destroy() seals both owned signals back into the lite-signal pool (H-12):
  reads freeze at their final value and mutations no-op.

## CSS contract

This primitive's painted attributes follow the canonical CSS contract in
`docs/CSS_CONTRACT.md`. See that doc for the cross-primitive taxonomy.
